newsitem.title: UK: Oil rally gathers pace amid fuel shortage fears.
newsitem.headline: Oil rally gathers pace amid fuel shortage fears.

text.p: World oil prices continued their torrid rally on Friday and traders expect further gains next week amid fears that world heating oil supplies will fall short this winter.
November futures for benchmark Brent Blend crude closed 14 cents up on the day at $23.88 a a barrel, extending this week's gains of more than $1 a barrel.
Crude prices have ridden higher on a wave of brisk buying of heating oil which hit post-Gulf War highs this week in the United States and Europe.

A spate of colder than normal weather in the U.S. northeast, the world's largest heating oil-consuming market, has exacerbated worries about U.S. heating oil inventories which are running about one third below last year's levels.
London traders expect the price of gas oil, a middle distillate used as heating fuel in Europe, could hit $300 a tonne if the winter is a cold one.
The October gas oil futures contract on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) closed at $245.50 a tonne on Friday.

"No one will be able to avoid a price spike if the weather's cold. A lot of consumers and companies dependent on distillates will suffer," said Bo Van Wijk, vice president of energy risk management at UBS in Zurich.

U.S. refineries have been pushing production to the limit in order to boost heating oil inventories, but traders have in recent weeks been shipping some of the oil across to Europe, where stocks are also low and prices higher.
